title: Why RAISE beats AUDIO as a Wordle opener
description:
Your first Wordle guess can't find the answer; its job is to shrink the list of 2,315 possible answers. Play an opener against every answer and sort them by the colors you'd see: each color pattern is a pile of words still possible. AUDIO makes only 89 piles, its likeliest result (one yellow A) leaves 435 words, and on average it leaves 184. RAISE splits the list into 132 piles, the biggest only 168, and leaves 61 on average: a third as many, from one guess.

Numbers checked in code against Wordle's original 2,315-word answer list (every opener played against every answer, plus 200,000 simulated games). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordle

beats.say: Raise or audio? One's three times better at Wordle.
And it's not the one with more vowels. Audio has four, and it still loses.
There are 2,315 possible answers. Your first guess won't find the word. Its job is to shrink that list.
So test your opener. Play it against all 2,315 answers, and sort them by the colors you'd get.
Every color pattern is a pile of words that are still possible. Play audio, and the likeliest result is one yellow A. That leaves 435 words.
Averaged over every answer, audio leaves you 184.
So vowels aren't the trick. The trick is more piles, and smaller ones.
Now try raise. It splits the list into 132 piles. Audio only made 89. And raise's biggest pile is just 168.
On average, raise leaves you 61 words. A third of audio's, from the same single guess.
A good first guess isn't a search. It's a sort.
